_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); semiconductor signals with NVIDIA's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (NVDA listed 1999-01-22)

pit_profile.why: 'NVIDIA Corporation invented the graphics processing unit, or GPU, in 1999.' 'The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change, evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.' 'We expect substantial competition from both Intel’s and AMD’s strategy of selling platform solutions, including integrating a CPU and a GPU on the same chip or same package, as evidenced by AMD’s announcement of its Fusion processors and Intel’s announcement of its family of CPUs codenamed Sandy Bridge.' 'Our business is cyclical in nature and has experienced severe downturns that have, and may in the future harm our business and financial results.' (FY2011 10-K); CYCLICAL on the 10-K's own words for its business (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical' reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json covers a CPU and a GPU integrated on one chip, so those words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -64.3%/yr (worst year FY02-FY11 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -6.9%/yr (Q1 FY12 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY09 ex-FY10 median

BULL.desc: EPS +4.9%/yr (FY02-FY11 ex-FY09 ex-FY10 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +147.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY11 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NVDA (retrospective, 2011-05-06) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 4.22x (95.5% downside to Bear $0.86 / +22.6% upside to Bull $23.69) | Adj composite 2.05 vs market 2.24: gap -0.19 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +136% above the EPP floor $8.17 (19x FY12E $0.43) | Conservative 2-yr case: -28.8% total (-14.4%/yr) | At 44.9x FY12E the 15% hurdle price $25.55 sits above the BULL case; revenue -9.8% YoY in Q4 FY11, forward revenues -6.2% to -4.4% (Q1 FY12 revenue guide (Q4 FY11 release)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
